scene: Inferno XXIX — Geri del Bello remembered; tenth bolgia falsifiers of metals afflicted by disease
story: While leaving the ninth bolgia, Dante delays, looking for Geri del Bello, a relative who died violently; Virgil says Geri passed by and gestured angrily because the death remains unavenged.
Virgil redirects Dante toward the tenth bolgia, the final ditch of Malebolge. Lamentations fill the air as they descend toward those punished for falsification.
The first group of falsifiers Dante sees are alchemists afflicted with a scabrous, leprosy-like disease; they sit together, scratching their damaged skin.

Two sufferers are identified as Griffolino d'Arezzo and Capocchio. Griffolino recounts deceiving Albero of Siena by claiming he could teach him to fly and suffering execution by fire; his punishment in Hell is attributed to falsifying metals.
Capocchio speaks as an imitator and falsifier of metals. Both individuals' testimony and visible affliction remain separate from the composition or identity of actual metals.
Dante and Virgil continue across the tenth bolgia; the encounters with other classes of falsifiers and their disputes belong to Canto XXX.
